headline: NYC RENT FREEZE
dek: A Manhattan judge upheld the Rent Guidelines Board’s two-year rent freeze and dismissed a landlord lawsuit, Gothamist reports.

nodes.text: The Rent Guidelines Board approves a two-year freeze, fulfilling one of Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s campaign pledges.
Landlords sue, saying the board ran a “sham” process that ignored owners’ rising expenses, and ask for a new vote. The mayor and city lawyers deny interfering and say the board decided independently.
Judge Brendan Lantry dismisses the suit, writing that the court lacked authority to overturn the freeze.

quotes.head: THE JUDGE
quotes.text: …may have detrimental impacts on the New York City residential real estate industry.
quotes.attr: Judge Brendan Lantry, on the freeze (via Gothamist)

quotes.head: TENANT LAWYERS
quotes.text: The law is clear that courts do not have the power to override the decisions of the Rent Guidelines Board.
quotes.attr: Ellen Davidson, Legal Aid Society (via Gothamist)

means.label: The freeze stays:
means.text: It stays in place for about 1 million rent-stabilized apartments.

means.label: A caveat:
means.text: Lantry said courts can’t override the board, but wrote that “to guarantee a rent freeze to millions of New Yorkers without the authority to do so, is irresponsible.”

means.label: What’s next:
means.text: Landlords’ attorney Randy Mastro didn’t say whether they’ll appeal.

sources: Sources: Gothamist, Nov. 25, 2026; The New York Times; New York Post, Nov. 25, 2026.
